question.text: Two cells having internal resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> are connected in parallel with the same polarity. The voltage across the battery terminals is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>. If the emf of the first cell is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>, then what is the emf of the second cell (in volt)?

solution.text:
Given that, the resultant voltage across the battery terminal=1.5 V



Clearly, 1.2 Volt Battery is Charging and another battery is discharging given,

1.2+0.2I=1.5

⇒I=32 A

E-0.4I=1.5

⇒E=1.5+0.4×32

⇒E=2.1 V
